hero.headline: States Prepare Antitrust Lawsuit to Block Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros.
hero.body:
Multiple U.S. states are preparing to file an antitrust lawsuit aimed at blocking Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, according to sources familiar with the matter. The effort represents a significant challenge to what would be one of the largest media consolidations in recent years.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta signaled the state's intent to challenge the deal, stating on social media that "Paramount/Warner Bros is not a done deal" and that the California Department of Justice has an open investigation. Bonta indicated he was in conversation with fellow state attorneys general about coordinating action against the $110 billion transaction.

Legal experts suggest state-level challenges pose a genuine threat. Alvaro Bedoya, who served on the Federal Trade Commission between 2022 and 2025, said he believed state attorneys general "have a shot at stopping it if they pool their resources." Bill Baer, former assistant attorney general in charge of the antitrust division at the Department of Justice, told the Guardian that "a combined lawsuit by state attorneys general presents a real threat," though he acknowledged it would be harder for states to succeed if federal regulators approve the deal.

The proposed merger has drawn opposition from entertainment industry workers and major organizations. The Writers Guild of America issued a statement opposing the deal, arguing that the loss of competition "would be a disaster for writers, consumers and the entire entertainment industry." Several U.S. senators, including Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal, have raised concerns about the consolidated power the deal would create, warning that one family would control Warner Bros., Paramount Plus, HBO, CBS News, CNN, and numerous other networks and channels.

Antitrust experts point to specific concerns. Bedoya noted there is "an even more compelling case that a whole lot of people are going to be put out of work," given that the combined company carries $79 billion in debt and will likely undertake significant cost-cutting measures including layoffs. Competition experts have also highlighted how merging HBO Max and Paramount Plus could reduce competition in the streaming market, though Paramount says it will maintain both the Warner Bros. and Paramount film studios.

Paramount's chief executive David Ellison has expressed confidence that the merger will pass regulatory review, claiming the combination "does not come close to hitting any of the metrics that would be problematic." Paramount has already completed at least two information requests from the Department of Justice, and the mandatory 10-day waiting period under federal antitrust law expired in February.

The state-level legal action would add another layer of complexity to an already complicated approval process. If multiple states file suit, the litigation could significantly delay or derail the transaction even if federal regulators ultimately allow it to proceed.

cards.headline: US forces intercept Iranian missiles and drones targeting Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
US military forces shot down Iranian missiles and drones launched toward the Strait of Hormuz, according to statements from the US military. The incident represents a fresh exchange of fire between the two nations as efforts to negotiate a lasting peace agreement have stalled.

The attack targeted the strategic waterway through which a significant portion of global oil shipments pass. US forces intercepted the Iranian drones and missiles before they could threaten commercial shipping traffic in the strait. Iran accused the United States of violating a ceasefire following the interception, though both sides have engaged in strikes as the current stalemate in peace negotiations continues.

The exchange comes as diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran have failed to produce progress. President Trump recently claimed that Iran had made a commitment not to develop nuclear weapons, but nuclear experts noted that Tehran has maintained this public position for more than 50 years. The renewed military confrontation underscores the fragility of the current situation despite ongoing diplomatic efforts.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical chokepoint for international energy markets, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow waterway. Any disruption to shipping in the area carries significant economic implications beyond the immediate military confrontation. The strait connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.

Neither side has indicated willingness to resume substantive negotiations following the latest incident. The pattern of military strikes and accusations of ceasefire violations suggests the current impasse could persist without a significant diplomatic breakthrough or shift in position by either Washington or Tehran.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit North Korea
cards.teaser: The trip marks a rare visit by the Chinese leader to the nuclear-armed neighbor, highlighting China's relationship with Pyongyang.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in his first visit since 2019. Both countries announced the trip Friday, a day after North Korea revealed a new facility for producing nuclear fuel.

The visit underscores China's central role in North Korea's international relations. As Pyongyang's most significant diplomatic and economic partner, China provides crucial support that helps North Korea withstand international sanctions. The trip allows North Korean leader Kim Jong Un to demonstrate confidence through his relationship with Beijing.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak spreads in East Africa
cards.teaser: The deadly virus is spreading through the region as questions emerge about whether China will help contain it.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak is spreading across East Africa, raising concerns about regional health infrastructure and international response. China is well positioned to assist in stopping the virus, according to health experts, and could fill a gap left by reduced US involvement in global health initiatives.

The outbreak presents a test of how international powers will respond to infectious disease threats in the region. China has expanded its presence in East Africa in recent years through infrastructure investment and development programs.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Spike as Talk of Demand Destruction Emerges
cards.teaser: Rising oil prices have revived discussion of demand destruction, when sustained high prices reduce commodity consumption.
cards.body:
Oil prices have risen sharply, prompting analysts and market observers to discuss the potential for demand destruction. The term refers to a sustained loss of demand for a commodity caused by elevated prices that force consumers and businesses to reduce consumption or find alternatives.

Demand destruction has been observed in previous oil price spikes, when high costs led drivers to reduce travel, businesses to cut fuel use, and industries to seek more efficient processes. The current price increases have raised questions about whether similar patterns will emerge.

cards.headline: 12 people shot near street festival in Toledo, Ohio
cards.body:
Police in Toledo, Ohio, are investigating a shooting that wounded at least 12 people near a community festival on Saturday. Authorities say two individuals fired weapons at each other during the incident.

The victims range in age from 14 to 61 years old. All were transported to nearby hospitals for treatment. Two of the wounded were in critical condition, according to Toledo deputy police chief Joe Heffernan.

Heffernan stated that it appeared two people fired weapons and were "probably shooting at each other." Police have not yet released information about the severity of all injuries or made any arrests related to the incident.

The shooting occurred near a street festival in the city, though police have not specified the exact location or time of the incident. Investigators believe the shooting was an exchange between two armed individuals rather than random gunfire directed at the crowd.

A search for the suspects continues as authorities work to identify those responsible for the shooting. Police have not released descriptions of the suspects or indicated whether they have identified any persons of interest in the case.

The incident adds to a troubling trend of gun violence near public gatherings. Ohio has experienced multiple mass shooting incidents in recent years, and gun violence at community events has become an increasing concern for law enforcement agencies across the United States. These incidents have prompted ongoing debates over security measures at festivals and other public gatherings.

Community organizers and city officials are likely to review safety protocols for future events in the wake of this shooting. The incident highlights the challenges law enforcement faces in protecting large crowds at outdoor festivals and public celebrations.

Police are urging anyone with information about the shooting to come forward. Investigators continue to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to locate the individuals responsible for firing the weapons.

The Toledo Police Department has not announced a timeline for when they expect to make arrests or provide additional details about the suspects. The investigation remains active and ongoing as authorities pursue leads in the case.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading.
cards.body:
Donald Trump pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who served nearly two years in prison for insider trading. Buyer was convicted of making illegal stock trades based on confidential information while working as a consultant and lobbyist after leaving office.

In 2023, Buyer was sentenced to 22 months in prison and ordered to forfeit more than $350,000 in illegal gains plus pay a $10,000 fine. He was released in 2025 before receiving the pardon this week.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St Petersburg during Russian economic forum
cards.teaser: Drone attacks on the Russian city overshadowed President Putin's flagship economic event.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drone attacks struck St Petersburg as Russia held a major economic forum in the city. The BBC's Russia editor witnessed Putin's flagship economic event being overshadowed by the strikes, which targeted the country's second-largest city during a gathering meant to showcase Russian economic prospects.

The attacks underscore Ukraine's expanding capability to strike deep within Russian territory. St Petersburg, Putin's hometown, has historically remained largely shielded from direct military action during the conflict.

cards.headline: Neo-Nazi party member reaches mayoral runoff in eastern German town
cards.teaser: A candidate from a neo-Nazi party advanced to a mayoral runoff, potentially breaking a pattern held since the fall of the Third Reich.
cards.body:
A candidate from a neo-Nazi party has advanced to the mayoral runoff in a small eastern German town, marking a significant moment in German politics. Since the end of World War II, German voters have consistently rejected far-right mayoral candidates at the ballot box.

The runoff election is scheduled for Sunday. Eastern Germany has emerged as a region of stronger support for far-right parties in recent years, distinguishing it from western areas of the country.

cards.headline: Armenia holds elections as Russia pressures pro-Western government
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeks a third term amid declining domestic support and Russian opposition.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is running for another term in national elections, though his support has declined domestically. His government's shift toward closer Western ties has created tension with Russia, Armenia's traditional security partner.

The election occurs amid regional instability and changing geopolitical alignments in the South Caucasus. Pashinyan's reorientation away from Moscow has strained Armenia's long-standing relationship with Russia.

cards.headline: Peru holds presidential runoff between moderated left and right-wing candidate
cards.teaser: Voters choose between two candidates as the country faces a surge in violence.
cards.body:
Peru is holding a presidential runoff election on Sunday between Keiko Fujimori, a right-wing candidate and daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, and Roberto Sánchez, a leftist congressman and former trade and tourism minister. Fujimori secured 17% in the first round while Sánchez took 12%, setting up a polarized left-right contest similar to Peru's 2021 election.

The election comes as Peru grapples with rising crime, chronic political instability, and corruption scandals. Voters are seeking stability after the country cycled through eight presidents in ten years. Security concerns and tackling inequality have become central issues in the divisive campaign.

cards.headline: Federal probe into California elections announced
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorney's office in California has announced an investigation into elections amid claims of fraud and slow ballot counting.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Justice sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as California's vote count continues at a slower-than-usual pace. The move comes as tensions rise over delayed results in races including the governor's contest.

The delay in ballot counting has prompted election-related claims on social media and from national figures, including assertions of election manipulation in California's primary races. State officials have rejected these allegations.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens as new votes tallied
cards.teaser: Yasmine Raman has closed the gap with Kevin Pratt in the Los Angeles mayor primary as additional ballots are counted.
cards.body:
New vote tallies show Raman gaining ground on Pratt in the race to determine who will face off against Mayor Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral election. Pratt's lead has eroded as election officials continue counting ballots.

Voters are awaiting news on both the mayoral race and the California governor's contest as the slow count continues. The two candidates are vying for a spot in the general election runoff against the incumbent mayor.

cards.headline: Hegseth criticizes European migration policy in Normandy speech
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Hegseth delivered remarks attacking European migration policies during a D-Day anniversary speech in Normandy.
cards.body:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew attention by using a D-Day commemoration speech in Normandy to criticize European migration policy. Speaking 82 years after allied forces launched their operation to liberate Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe, Hegseth employed language comparing contemporary migration to a beach invasion.

His remarks represented a notable shift from traditional messaging at military anniversary ceremonies, which typically focus on historical remembrance rather than current policy disputes.

cards.headline: Research shows bumblebees can solve problems like larger animals
cards.teaser: New research suggests bumblebees may be capable of spontaneously solving problems in ways similar to chimps and elephants.
cards.body:
Bumblebees can use tools to solve problems, demonstrating cognitive abilities comparable to much larger animals. In experiments based on a classic test from a century ago—where chimpanzees learned to stack boxes to reach an out-of-reach banana—bumblebees showed they could solve the puzzle spontaneously.

This finding places bumblebees among an exclusive group of species capable of this level of insight, joining chimpanzees, elephants, crows, and other primates. The research suggests that advanced problem-solving abilities are not limited to animals with large brains, revealing remarkable cognitive flexibility in these tiny insects.

cards.headline: UK defence plan delayed ahead of NATO summit
cards.teaser: British lawmakers say delays to the Defence Investment Plan undermine the country's credibility.
cards.body:
Members of Parliament have criticized delays to the UK Defence Investment Plan, arguing the postponements undermine British credibility with allies. The plan is now scheduled for release ahead of a NATO summit early next month.

The government's defence spending plans have featured prominently on newspaper front pages, with concerns about the impact of the delayed publication on the UK's defence commitments to its NATO partners.

cards.headline: Retailers Report Shift in Consumer Spending Patterns
cards.teaser: Retailers are observing changes in consumer behavior, including reduced gas purchases and fewer premium purchases.
cards.body:
Major retailers are reporting shifts in consumer spending as shoppers adjust their habits. Observations include customers filling gas tanks less frequently and cutting back on non-essential items and premium options.

The changes suggest consumers are responding to economic pressures by rethinking discretionary spending. Retailers have noted the adjustments across multiple categories as shoppers prioritize essential purchases and seek ways to reduce costs.

cards.headline: CaaStle CEO Remained in Position After Fraud Confession
cards.teaser: Fashion tech startup CaaStle's board allowed CEO Christine Hunsicker to stay in charge after she admitted to defrauding the company.
cards.body:
Christine Hunsicker, CEO of fashion tech startup CaaStle, confessed to defrauding the company but was permitted by the board to remain in her leadership role. The final months of CaaStle's operations included fake audits, stock buybacks, and a damage control strategy.

Hunsicker led the damage control efforts despite being the executive who had defrauded the company. The board's decision to retain her as CEO raised questions about corporate governance at the startup during its closing period.

cards.headline: CEOs and Professors Deploy AI Twins to Handle Meetings and Questions
cards.teaser: Business leaders and academics are using AI versions of themselves to answer questions and attend meetings.
cards.body:
Chief executives and Harvard professors have begun using artificial intelligence twins as a productivity tool. The AI versions are designed to answer questions and attend meetings on behalf of the actual person.

Proponents describe the technology as a way to manage time more efficiently by delegating routine interactions to AI systems trained to respond in their voice and style. The practice represents a growing trend of executives using automation to handle communication and scheduling tasks.

cards.headline: WWE Shareholder Lawsuit Trial Canceled
cards.teaser: A trial for a WWE shareholder lawsuit has been removed from the court schedule.
cards.body:
The trial for a lawsuit filed by WWE shareholders has been canceled and removed from the court calendar. The cancellation spares WWE leadership, including executives who were expected to face questioning, from immediate courtroom proceedings.

The lawsuit related to claims brought by shareholders regarding company actions. The removal from the court schedule represents a significant development in the case, though the reasons for the cancellation were not detailed in available court filings.

cards.headline: Debt Collectors Face Verbal Abuse and Threats From Callers
cards.teaser: As more Americans fall behind on bills, debt collection workers report enduring verbal abuse and violence threats.
cards.body:
People working in debt collection are experiencing increased verbal abuse and threats of violence from the individuals they contact. The hostile interactions occur as more Americans take on debt and fall behind on bill payments.

Debt collectors face a difficult work environment as they attempt to recover overdue payments while managing aggressive responses from stressed borrowers. The rise in delinquencies has corresponded with an increase in confrontational calls.

hero.headline: OpenAI introduces Lockdown Mode to block prompt injection attacks
hero.body:
OpenAI Delays Adult Mode Launch as Company Faces Competing Priorities

OpenAI has postponed its planned "adult mode" for ChatGPT to focus on more urgent development work, the company announced this week. The decision comes after the startup's chief executive Sam Altman had previously committed to rolling out the feature alongside age verification tools.

"We're pushing out the launch of adult mode so we can focus on work that is a higher priority for more users right now, including gains in intelligence, personality improvements, personalisation, and making the experience more proactive," OpenAI said in a statement.

The delay reflects shifting priorities at the company, which serves more than 900 million ChatGPT users globally. Since announcing adult mode plans last October, Altman has declared a "code red" initiative to improve ChatGPT's capabilities amid intensifying competition from Google and Anthropic.

While adult mode launch has been postponed, OpenAI is rolling out age prediction technology to determine whether users are under 18. When the system identifies a minor, it activates enhanced safety features that limit exposure to graphic violence and sexually explicit roleplay content. In the United Kingdom, OpenAI must implement strict age verification for any pornographic images ChatGPT generates under the Online Safety Act.

On the principle behind the delayed feature, OpenAI stated: "We still believe in the principle of treating adults like adults, but getting the experience right will take more time."

The announcement comes as OpenAI navigates broader organizational challenges. This week, Caitlin Kalinowski, head of hardware in OpenAI's robotics division, resigned over concerns regarding the company's Pentagon partnership.

Kalinowski cited worries about domestic surveillance of US citizens and AI-guided autonomous weapons systems. "This wasn't an easy call," she wrote on social media. "AI has an important role in national security. But surveillance of Americans without judicial oversight and lethal autonomy without human authorization are lines that deserved more deliberation than they got."

Kalinowski emphasized respect for company leadership while expressing frustration with the pace of execution. "My issue is that the announcement was rushed without the guardrails defined. It's a governance concern first and foremost. These are too important for deals or announcements to be rushed," she explained in a follow-up post.

The Pentagon deal had drawn immediate scrutiny. OpenAI later amended the contract to explicitly exclude domestic surveillance applications after Altman acknowledged the agreement appeared "opportunistic and sloppy."

An OpenAI spokesperson responded to the resignation concerns: "We believe our agreement with the Pentagon creates a workable path for responsible national security uses of AI while making clear our red lines: no domestic surveillance and no autonomous weapons. We recognise that people have strong views about these issues and we will continue to engage in discussion with employees, government, civil society and communities around the world."

cards.headline: Fossils reveal three-foot scorpion that lived 415 million years ago
cards.teaser: Scientists identified the largest scorpion species ever discovered, measuring over three feet long with six-inch pincers.
cards.body:
Researchers analyzing 415-million-year-old fossils from the Devonian Period identified what they describe as the largest scorpion species to have existed. The creature measured over three feet in length and possessed pincers stretching six inches across.

The discovery provides new information about apex predators that lived in ancient Britain hundreds of millions of years ago. The Natural History Museum and other scientific institutions contributed to the research documenting the massive arthropod that inhabited Earth long before dinosaurs appeared.

cards.headline: Game developer announces Stellar Blade sequel Blood Rain
cards.teaser: Shift Up revealed Blood Rain, the sequel to action game Stellar Blade, though the announcement drew scrutiny over alleged use of generative AI.
cards.body:
Developer Shift Up announced Blood Rain, a sequel to its action game Stellar Blade. The reveal trailer showcased combat mechanics and large-scale city environments that the company says will define the new title.

The announcement attracted criticism after observers identified what they described as signs of generative AI in promotional materials. Multiple gaming news outlets reported that elements of the reveal appeared to contain AI-generated imagery, raising questions about the production tools used in the game's marketing campaign.

cards.headline: Remastered Godzilla brawler coming to PlayStation 5 and Switch 2
cards.teaser: Atari plans to release a remaster of 2002's Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee on current and next-generation consoles this November.
cards.body:
Atari announced a remastered version of Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, a fighting game originally released in 2002 on GameCube. The updated version will launch on PlayStation 5 and Nintendo's upcoming Switch 2 console in November.

The kaiju brawler lets players control giant monsters in destructible city environments. The remaster marks the return of a title that has been unavailable on modern platforms for over two decades. Atari also revealed plans for a separate Barbie game collection, though details on that project were not provided.

cards.headline: Vampire Survivors confirmed for Switch 2 with new expansion
cards.teaser: Developer poncle announced a Nintendo Switch 2 version of its hit roguelike game alongside a new downloadable expansion called Legacy of the Bloodmoon.
cards.body:
Poncle announced that Vampire Survivors will launch natively on Nintendo Switch 2. The developer also unveiled Legacy of the Bloodmoon, a new expansion for the roguelike action game.

To support its growth, poncle plans to establish a Japan-based development team led by Sawaki Takeyasu, who created El Shaddai. The expansion signals the studio's commitment to continuing development across multiple platforms.

cards.headline: Scientists removed from diabetes conference for handing out journal articles
cards.teaser: Conference organizers ejected multiple researchers, including an ADA journal editor and former president, for distributing journal reprints.
cards.body:
Several scientists, including Steven Kahn, editor-in-chief of an American Diabetes Association journal, and Desmond Schatz, a former ADA president, were ejected from a diabetes conference for distributing reprints of published journal articles.

The incident raises questions about conference policies that would prohibit the distribution of peer-reviewed research materials at a professional gathering.

cards.headline: New telescope facility to begin decade-long survey of solar system objects
cards.teaser: A new observatory is months away from starting a 10-year project to catalog millions of previously unseen objects within the solar system.
cards.body:
An astronomical survey facility will begin operations within months to identify and track millions of objects in the solar system that have never been observed. The project is designed to run for a full decade, systematically mapping the region.

Scientists estimate that millions of asteroids, comets, and other bodies orbit the sun without having been detected by existing telescopes. The new facility's survey aims to create a comprehensive catalog of these objects, expanding knowledge of the solar system's composition and structure.

hero.headline: Nelly Korda shares lead at US Women's Open after third round
hero.teaser: Nelly Korda moved into a share of the lead while England's Charley Hull surged into contention at the US Women's Open.
hero.body:
Nelly Kord carded a four-under par 67 to move into a share of the lead after the third round of the US Women's Open. England's Charley Hull fired a 65 to storm into contention heading into the final round.

Kord's steady play kept her at the top of the leaderboard as the tournament enters its final day. Hull's impressive round vaulted her into position to challenge for the championship in Sunday's conclusion.

The third round produced competitive golf from both players as they jockey for position in one of women's golf's most prestigious events. Kord maintained her position through consistent scoring, while Hull's hot round on the course demonstrated her ability to make a run up the leaderboard.

Hull's 65 represents a significant effort to position herself within striking distance for the final round. The English golfer took advantage of favorable conditions to post one of the day's best scores. Her performance suggests she will be a formidable challenger when play resumes for the championship conclusion.

Kord's approach to the third round emphasized steady play rather than aggressive scoring. The four-under round kept pace with the competition and preserved her position at the top. Her consistency through three rounds demonstrates the mental and technical discipline required to contend in major championships.

The leaderboard entering the final round shapes up as competitive heading into Sunday. Kord and whoever else shares the lead will face the pressure of defending their position over the course of eighteen holes. Hull's position following her impressive 65 means she will apply pressure to those ahead of her.

The US Women's Open is one of golf's four major championships and represents a significant achievement for any player who can win it. The third round typically separates contenders from those who cannot maintain their level through the tournament's most demanding stretches. Both Kord and Hull have demonstrated they belong among the championship contenders.

Kord's experience playing in major championships at the highest levels of professional golf provides her with valuable perspective heading into the final round. Hull's sudden movement up the leaderboard on the back of her 65 brings fresh energy to the competition.

The final round of the US Women's Open will determine which player can sustain their performance when the stakes are highest. Kord will look to protect her position while Hull will attempt to convert her third-round momentum into a championship performance. The conclusion promises to be compelling as both players test their skills against the course and their competitors.

The championship will be decided over eighteen holes on Sunday as one player emerges victorious in one of women's golf's marquee events.

cards.headline: Golden Tempo wins Belmont Stakes to complete Triple Crown
cards.teaser: Golden Tempo captured the third leg of the Triple Crown five weeks after winning the Kentucky Derby.
cards.body:
Golden Tempo won the Belmont Stakes on Saturday at Saratoga Race Course, completing the Triple Crown five weeks after winning the Kentucky Derby. With jockey Jose Ortiz in the saddle, Golden Tempo charged down the stretch to secure victory at 6-1 odds, finishing ahead of Commandment in second place.

The triumph marks another historic achievement for trainer Cherie DeVaux, who becomes part of an exclusive group to train a Triple Crown winner. Favorite Renegade finished third in the 158th running of the prestigious race.

cards.headline: Golden Knights defeat Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime after squandering four-goal lead
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights recovered from blowing a 4-0 lead to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final on Saturd.
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights beat the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, securing a 2-1 series lead. Defenseman Shea Theodore scored the winner at 5:38 of the second overtime period, with the goal deflecting off goalie Brandon Bussi's skate.

The Hurricanes mounted a remarkable comeback from a four-goal deficit to force the game into overtime. Mitch Marner recorded the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history during the contest. Theodore's goal prevented what could have been a devastating loss for Vegas after they squandered their early advantage.

cards.headline: Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski throws fastest pitch by starter since 2008
cards.teaser: Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski fired a 103.7 mph pitch during Saturday's game against the Rockies.
cards.body:
Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski reached 103.7 mph on a fastball during Saturday's game against the Colorado Rockies. The velocity marks the fastest pitch thrown by a starting pitcher since MLB began tracking such data in 2008.

The achievement underscores Misiorowski's powerful arsenal as a Brewers starter. His fastball surpassed the previous record held by all other starting pitchers throughout the nearly two-decade tracking era.

cards.headline: Gabriel Bonfim defeats former champion Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Welterweight Gabriel Bonfim dominated former champion Belal Muhammad at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
Gabriel Bonfim improved to 20-1 with a dominant performance on Saturday night at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas, defeating former champion Belal Muhammad, who dropped to 24-6. Throughout the bout, Bonfim displayed confidence and composure, frequently smiling and laughing as he controlled the action.

The victory marks a significant breakthrough for the welterweight, who secured a notable win over a former title holder. Bonfim's commanding performance established him as an emerging contender in the division.

cards.headline: Chase Elliott to lead Hendrick Motorsports at Michigan after qualifying
cards.teaser: Chase Elliott will lead Hendrick Motorsports to the green flag at Michigan International Speedway on Sunday.
cards.body:
Chase Elliott secured the top qualifying position for Hendrick Motorsports ahead of Sunday's NASCAR race at Michigan International Speedway. The qualifying results set the starting order for the weekend race.

Elliott's performance in qualifying gives him the pole position for the Michigan race. The results position Hendrick Motorsports favorably as the team prepares for Sunday's competition at the track.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi rested as Argentina, Brazil, Germany, Belgium and Portugal win World Cup warm-ups
cards.teaser: Argentina rested Lionel Messi against Honduras as several nations won warm-up games prior to the World Cup.
cards.body:
Argentina rested Lionel Messi in their friendly against Honduras as teams prepared for the World Cup. Brazil, Germany, Belgium and Portugal all won their warm-up matches ahead of the tournament.

The pre-World Cup friendlies gave teams an opportunity to fine-tune their preparations while managing player workloads before the competition began.

hero.headline: Bruce Springsteen Opens Music Center in New Jersey
hero.teaser: The rock musician performed with Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy at a concert celebrating the new facility at Monmouth University.
hero.body:
Bruce Springsteen inaugurated the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music at Monmouth University with a special preview concert ahead of the facility's official June 13 opening. The event, called "Music America," featured performances from the rock legend alongside Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy.

The new center will showcase guitars and other musical memorabilia related to American music history. The concert served as an early glimpse of the venue for attendees before its formal launch date. The star-studded performance gave visitors an opportunity to experience the space and its inaugural programming.

Springsteen, who was born and raised in New Jersey, has maintained deep ties to the state's vibrant music scene throughout his career. The decision to locate his center at Monmouth University reflects the strong connection between the artist and the region. The university, situated in the musician's home state, provided an appropriate setting for a facility dedicated to celebrating American music.

The center represents a significant cultural addition to New Jersey's arts landscape. By housing guitars and memorabilia from Springsteen's career and broader American music history, the facility aims to serve as both a museum and educational resource. The preview concert demonstrated the venue's capacity to host major performances and events.

The June 13 opening marks an important milestone for the institution. The center's establishment comes as recognition of Springsteen's decades-long influence on music and culture. His work, which has frequently drawn inspiration from New Jersey themes and settings, has earned him a devoted following and significant cultural impact.

The "Music America" concert brought together three distinct musical acts representing different genres and eras. Bon Jovi, another New Jersey native, and Public Enemy, the influential hip-hop group, joined Springsteen for what organizers billed as a celebration of American musical diversity. The collaboration underscored the center's mission to honor various traditions within American music.

Monmouth University's selection as the home for the center reflects the institution's commitment to arts and culture programming. The university's location in Long Branch, New Jersey, places it within the region that has been central to Springsteen's artistic identity and career. The partnership between the musician and the university creates an educational and cultural resource for students and the broader public.

The opening of the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music adds to New Jersey's cultural infrastructure. By combining performance space, exhibition areas for memorabilia, and educational opportunities, the facility aims to engage audiences with American music history. The center joins other institutions across the state dedicated to preserving and celebrating the region's significant contributions to music and the arts.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Thanks Supporters After 60 Minutes Dismissal
cards.teaser: The veteran correspondent posted a message to fans following his firing by the program's new executive producer.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley thanked supporters on Instagram after being dismissed from 60 Minutes. In a lengthy statement, the veteran correspondent accused CBS News executives of instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting and said the network was silencing employees.

Pelley emphasized that 60 Minutes built its decades-long reputation as America's top-rated program on integrity and quality journalism. Meanwhile, remaining correspondents Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim announced they would continue with the program under new executive producer Nick Bilton's leadership.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Marry in Sicily as Elton John Performs
cards.teaser: Pop star Dua Lipa and actor Callum Turner married in Sicily on Saturday, with Elton John performing his song "Your Song" at the ceremony.
cards.body:
Pop star Dua Lipa and actor Callum Turner married in Sicily on Saturday, with Elton John performing his song "Your Song" at the ceremony. The wedding took place in Palermo, where the couple brought what sources described as vintage glamour to their nuptials.

The high-profile event divided residents of Palermo. One local told reporters they could understand such disruption "if it was for the pope," reflecting tensions over the attention the wedding brought to the city. The couple had previously held London nuptials before the Sicily ceremony.

Lipa, known for hits including "Levitating" and "Don't Start Now," and Turner, who has appeared in films including the "Fantastic Beasts" franchise, began dating in 2024. The Sicily wedding included what sources described as a sweet nod to their first meeting, though specific details of that reference were not disclosed.

Elton John's participation as wedding performer added star power to an already notable guest list. The British singer-songwriter has performed at numerous celebrity weddings throughout his career, making him a sought-after addition to major entertainment industry events.

The wedding follows a trend of celebrity couples choosing Italian destinations for their ceremonies. Sicily, the Mediterranean island known for its historic architecture and coastal scenery, has become an increasingly popular location for high-profile weddings in recent years. The couple's choice to hold ceremonies in both London and Sicily reflects a growing practice among international celebrities of celebrating marriages in multiple locations.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Premieres Duet With the Cure's Robert Smith
cards.teaser: The pop singer revealed a collaboration with the veteran rock musician during a surprise performance at a Spanish music festival.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo surprised fans at Primavera Sound festival by unveiling a duet with the Cure's Robert Smith. The collaboration, titled "What's Wrong With Me," was performed live as Smith joined Rodrigo onstage for the premiere.

The duet appears on Rodrigo's forthcoming album, arriving within days of the festival performance. The partnership marks an unexpected collaboration between the pop star and the veteran rock musician, blending their distinct musical styles on the new track.

cards.headline: Ye Performs in Netherlands Despite Protests
cards.teaser: The rapper took the stage for thousands of fans after a Dutch court allowed the concerts to proceed.
cards.body:
Ye performed for thousands of fans in the Netherlands after a Dutch court rejected an attempt to stop the concerts. A Jewish group had sought to block the shows, citing antisemitic remarks the rapper had previously made, but the judge ruled the concerts could proceed.

The decision came amid ongoing controversy surrounding Ye, formerly known as Kanye West. Despite the protests and legal challenge, thousands attended the concert. The court's ruling allowed the European tour dates to move forward as planned.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center Lawsuit Against Musician Dismissed
cards.teaser: A judge threw out the venue's case against an artist who canceled a performance over the facility's name change.
cards.body:
A judge dismissed the Kennedy Center's lawsuit against musician Chuck Redd, who canceled a Christmas Eve show after the venue added Trump's name to its title. The court ruled in favor of Redd, who had refused to perform at the renamed facility.

The Kennedy Center had sued Redd over the cancellation. The musician's decision to pull out of the performance came in response to the venue's name change. The judge's ruling ends the legal dispute between the Washington performance hall and the artist.

cards.headline: Charlie Puth Cancels Orlando Concert Due to Illness
cards.teaser: The pop singer called off his Saturday performance, saying he was instructed to rest.
cards.body:
Charlie Puth announced on Instagram that he must cancel his Saturday concert in Orlando, Florida due to illness. The singer expressed his devastation over the cancellation, stating he had been sick for several days.

Puth described himself as "heartbroken" about missing the show and noted that medical advice required him to rest and skip the performance.

hero.headline: Trump approval ratings hit new lows ahead of midterms
hero.teaser: The president faces growing tensions with Senate Republicans as his approval numbers decline.
hero.body:
President Trump is scheduled to appear on NBC's Meet the Press Sunday following a week that saw his approval ratings reach new lows. The interview comes as midterm elections approach and tensions between the president and Senate Republicans have spilled into public view.

Multiple recent polls show Trump's overall approval rating has dropped significantly. According to Reuters-Ipsos, Strength in Numbers-Verasight and AP-NORC surveys, the president's approval hovered in the mid-30s, ranging from 33% to 36%. An NBC News poll found his personal approval rating at 37%, with 63% disapproving, marking a second-term low.

The economy remains a critical weakness. An AP-NORC poll found that Trump's handling of the economy fell to just 30% approval, down from 38% in March. Only 23% approve of how he is handling the cost of living, while 76% disapprove. Seven in 10 Americans described the economy as poor and believe the country is headed in the wrong direction.

Trump's signature immigration policies are also creating political headwinds for Republican candidates. A Reuters-Ipsos poll found that 52% of Americans said they were less likely to support a candidate who backs Trump's approach to deportations, compared to just 42% who said they were more likely to support such a candidate. Support for his immigration policy has dropped from 50% in the weeks after his January 2025 inauguration to 40% currently. The divide is even sharper among independent voters, with 57% preferring candidates who oppose Trump's deportation approach.

Foreign policy challenges compound these problems. Two-thirds of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the war with Iran, with only one-third approving. A majority of 61% said the US should not take any further military action in Iran.

Despite these broad struggles, Trump maintains significant support among his party base. The NBC poll found that 83% of Republicans still approve of Trump, though this represents a 4-point decline from earlier in the year. Among Republicans, 52% strongly approve of his economic handling, down from 58% previously.

The political landscape presents stark challenges for Republican candidates defending their congressional majorities. Two-thirds of Americans believe the country is on the wrong track, compared to just one-third who believe it is moving in the right direction. The economy continues to be the top issue for voters at 29%, followed by threats to democracy at 24%.

There is one area where Trump and Republicans find stronger support. Three-quarters of Americans support government-issued photo ID requirements for voting, and 61% believe such documents should include proof of citizenship.

As Trump prepares for his Sunday interview, these polling numbers underscore the political headwinds his party faces in the approaching midterm elections.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into potential election fraud in California's elections.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office announced Saturday that it has launched an investigation into election fraud allegations related to California's elections. The probe comes amid ongoing vote counting in multiple statewide and local races across the state.

The announcement follows claims from conservative figures, including President Trump, about irregularities in California's vote-counting process. The investigation will examine specific allegations of fraud, though federal prosecutors have not detailed which claims prompted the inquiry or what evidence they are reviewing.

cards.headline: Former House Speaker McCarthy questions California vote counting
cards.teaser: Kevin McCarthy echoed President Trump's unsubstantiated claims about California's election process.
cards.body:
Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy told radio hosts Friday that California voters were losing faith in the state's vote-counting process. His comments echoed unsubstantiated claims of election fraud pushed by conservatives, including President Trump, amid ongoing delays in the state's primary election results.

California's slower counting pace stems from its system of verifications designed to protect against fraud and ensure every vote is counted accurately. Election experts say the process is working as intended, processing mail ballots and provisional votes according to standard procedures.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters should not receive pardons or compensation
cards.teaser: The former vice president said those who assaulted officers or vandalized property during the Capitol attack should get no clemency.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence said Friday that Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property, or sought to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election should not be pardoned by President Trump. Pence told HBO's Real Time that such individuals should never receive financial compensation.

The remarks reflect Pence's ongoing disagreement with Trump over how to characterize the 2021 attack on the Capitol. Trump has granted pardons to some Jan. 6 participants, describing certain rioters as political prisoners. Pence, who was presiding over the electoral count when rioters breached the building, has maintained that those who committed violence should face consequences.

cards.headline: White House AI policy adviser to step down at end of month
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this mo.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, a senior policy adviser on artificial intelligence at the White House, confirmed Saturday that he will leave his position at the end of this month. Krishnan, a tech investor who became a key figure in the Trump administration's AI efforts, played a central role in developing strategic plans aligned with the president's goals for artificial intelligence policy.

Krishnan's departure comes as the administration continues to shape its approach to regulating and advancing AI technology. His tenure focused on coordinating between government agencies and private sector partners to establish frameworks for AI development and deployment. The White House has positioned artificial intelligence as a priority area for both economic competitiveness and national security.

The timing of Krishnan's exit raises questions about continuity in the administration's AI policy efforts. As one of the most visible advisers on technology issues, his work influenced how the government engages with rapidly evolving AI capabilities. The administration has not yet announced a replacement or indicated whether the role will be restructured.

Krishnan brought experience from both Silicon Valley investment circles and technology development to his government position. His background in the private sector informed his approach to balancing innovation incentives with regulatory oversight. The White House relied on his expertise to navigate complex technical questions about AI safety, data privacy, and algorithmic accountability.

The departure adds to broader personnel shifts within the administration as it approaches the midpoint of Trump's term. White House officials have not detailed Krishnan's post-government plans or specified his exact departure date beyond indicating it will occur by the end of the month. The administration's AI strategy will now proceed under different leadership as technology policy remains a contested area between government regulators and industry advocates.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor after serving in the Biden administration, where she represented a congressional district before joining the federal government.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in the United States.

cards.headline: Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: The latest results show Republican Hilton and Democrat Becerra ahead in the race to replace Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's governor primary as votes continue to be counted. Becerra's campaign has made a remarkable turnaround after polling at just 3% in late March. If he wins the general election, he would become California's first Latino governor since 1875.

The top two finishers will advance to face each other in November to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. California's top-two primary system places all candidates on the same ballot regardless of party affiliation. Other candidates in the race include Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, along with Republican Chad Bianco.
